Haji Abdollah Khan Gharagozloo (Sa'ed al-Saltaneh, later Sardar Akram and Amir Nezam) was a senior Qajar military commander, provincial administrator, landholder, author, minister, Majles deputy, and international traveler. In addition to his reports on Sarakhs and Khuzestan, his surviving Mecca travelogue from 1319 AH records a journey through the Caucasus, Ottoman and Egyptian transport networks to Jeddah and Mecca, detailed observations of pilgrimage administration, a severe cholera outbreak, and a meeting with the Sharif of Mecca. His writings also refer to earlier European travel, including Rome, Paris, St. Petersburg and Moscow, although the separate Europe travelogue itself has not yet been located. He died in Hamadan on 23 Sha'ban 1334 AH (1916 CE).

The exact intermediate genealogy connecting him to the later documented Hajilou trunk remains unresolved.
